children: CALGARY, AB, Nov. 25, 2026 /CNW/ -- CanAsia Energy Corp. ("CanAsia" or the "Company") (CEC – TSXV) reports 2026 third quarter consolidated financial and operating results.

The Company is today filing its unaudited consolidated financial statements as at and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and related management's discussion and analysis (the "MD&A") with Canadian securities regulatory authorities.  Copies of these documents may be obtained online at
or the Company's website,

Commenting today on CanAsia's 2026 third quarter results, President and CEO Jeff Chisholm stated: "We are obviously pleased with the results from the Andora sale and are now looking forward to the signing of petroleum concession L8/66, onshore Thailand, that will occur on November 30, 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand."
HIGHLIGHTS

As at September 30, 2026, the assets and liabilities of Andora Energy Corporation ("Andora") were classified as held for sale ($37.0 million of assets and $11.6 million of liabilities) and the results of Andora were presented as discontinued operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, in accordance with IFRS 5.

Subsequent to September 30, 2026, on October 30, 2026 the Company completed the sale of all of the issued and outstanding shares of Andora to Logan Oil Corp. (the "Purchaser"), an arm's length party, and received cash proceeds of $29.4 million, representing a base purchase price of $30 million, plus an estimated net debt adjustment of $1.4 million, less a $2 million holdback pending finalization of the net debt amount (the "Andora Transaction"). The Purchaser has also agreed to pay the Company contingent consideration of $10 million upon achieving first oil sales from Andora's Sawn Lake project, subject to certain conditions, and CanAsia will be entitled to receive an aggregate maximum payment of up to $15 million under a conditional payment agreement entered into between the Company, the Purchaser and Andora effective as of the closing of the Andora Transaction. See "Recent Developments" in the MD&A.

On October 5, 2026, CanAsia was formally notified of the award of a petroleum concession for Thailand Onshore Exploration Block No. L8/66 to CanAsia and its joint venture partner Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd. ("POES"), pursuant to the onshore Thailand 25th licensing round. CanAsia will hold a non-operated 30% participating interest and POES will be the operator, subject to entering into a definitive concession agreement.
On November 12, 2026, the board of directors of CanAsia approved a return of capital of $17 million, payable on November 26, 2026 pro rata to shareholders of record on November 19, 2026.

As at September 30, 2026, Andora had received a total of $9.5 million in funding pursuant to the Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (the "KIGAM Agreement") with the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources in relation to Andora's heavy oil project in Sawn Lake, Alberta, of which $7.0 million was held as restricted cash (non-current) and included in assets held for sale. Total spending under the project was $0.8 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
CanAsia had a working capital deficit of $2.3 million, no long-term debt and shareholders' equity of $23.1 million at September 30, 2026.

Common shares outstanding were 113.6 million at September 30, 2026 and 122.5 million at November 24, 2026, following the exercise of 8,825,000 outstanding stock options subsequent to September 30, 2026. The Company does not currently have any stock options outstanding.

Net loss was $0.4 million ($0.00 per share) in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.7 million ($0.01 per share) in the third quarter of 2025. Loss from continuing operations was $32 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. The third quarter of 2026 included a gain on derecognition of decommissioning provision of $0.5 million relating to Indonesia, partially offset by higher general and administrative expense. Loss from discontinued operations was $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Net income was $17.8 million ($0.16 per share) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a net loss of $2.3 million ($0.02 per share) in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included income from discontinued operations of $19.4 million, which benefited from an impairment recovery of $19.9 million related to the Sawn Lake exploration and evaluation assets recognized in the second quarter of 2026 as a result of the KIGAM Agreement, and a $0.3 million recovery on the derecognition of the natural gas pipeline tariff onerous provision.

Cash flow used in operating activities from continuing operations was $0.1 million ($0.00 per share) in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. Cash flow used in operating activities from continuing operations in the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to general and administrative expense of $0.5 million, partially offset by changes in non-cash working capital of $0.3 million. Cash flow used in operating activities of discontinued operations was $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to cash flow used of $0.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

General and administrative expense from continuing operations was $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. General and administrative expense is comprised primarily of expenses related to personnel and premises, external services, and public company costs.

Personnel and premises costs were $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. These costs include salaries and benefits for employees, and fees incurred for consultants. They also include rent and other office costs related to the Company's Calgary office.

External service costs were $0.2 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025. These costs are mainly related to professional fees for legal, audit, tax services, information technology and engineering.

Public company costs were $0.1 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025. These costs were incurred for maintaining the Company's status as a public company and mainly related to shareholder reporting and meetings, TSXV fees, transfer agent, insurance and directors' fees.

Operating expenses of Andora, included in discontinued operations, were a recovery of $20 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 compared to an expense of $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2025, and $0.2 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $0.5 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. These expenses were incurred to restart and maintain the assets of Andora's SAGD project facility and wellpair at Sawn Lake Central.

The natural gas pipeline tariff agreement which was entered into between Andora and a third party in 2018 with a commencement date of June 1, 2023 was recognized as an onerous contract under IAS 37 since the operation at Sawn Lake is shut-in. The natural gas pipeline tariff provision of $0.5 million (current and non-current) as at September 30, 2026 was included in liabilities associated with assets held for sale. During the second quarter of 2026, the Company reassessed the expected period during which the contract is anticipated to remain onerous and adjusted the provision to account for the revised onerous period, resulting in a recovery of $0.3 million included in income from discontinued operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

The decommissioning provision relating to the legacy subsidiaries of POEH which had held interests in the East Jabung Production Sharing Contract in Indonesia of $0.5 million was derecognized during the third quarter of 2026, resulting in a gain of $0.5 million. The decommissioning provision of $1.9 million as at September 30, 2026 pertaining to Andora's interests in Sawn Lake was included in liabilities associated with assets held for sale.
OUTLOOK

Activities over the next quarter are anticipated to be comprised of incorporating and interpreting newly received seismic and well data over the new Thailand concession and acquiring new 3D seismic over the most prospective portion, in addition to various business development activities.
